title: survey-filters
intention: THE JUDGES BEFORE THE JUDGED, SECOND INSTANCE (constrain-filters filed edge (b) — 'pattern, not rule, until a second instance proves it'; this is that instance): install the build_inspector filters that will gate the survey brick's output BEFORE the survey module exists. Two filters, minimal by design, each encoding a measured failure that PRECEDES the module: (1) survey_holdings_resolve — every holding in a berthed survey packet names an address that resolves on disk; a holding the world doesn't hold is the state-reported-from-records failure wearing an inventory's costume. (2) survey_coverage_complete — a survey packet declares what it SOUGHT (non-empty; an empty sought means the sweep never ran wide), and every absence claim carries the MEASURE that established it (an absence without its measure is the '0 of 13' word-grep). Both run through the packet jurisdiction the wire built, AND both are exposed as a pure judge (judge_survey, owned by the inspector) that the future survey berth door COMPOSES — one implementation, two mouths. The judge lives in the inspector and survey imports it, never the reverse.
why: Survey's ONE question is 'what already exists that bears on this request?' — and its two failure classes were measured before the module: (a) HOLDINGS THAT AREN'T THERE — 2026-07-26/27, system state reported from records, wrong about the world three times (device_census's own seeding failures); and 2026-07-28, stone 1's parallel charter-glob roster: a build begun without surveying the settled territory, so the survey that should have found cairn/tools/orient never ran. (b) ABSENCES WITHOUT THEIR MEASURE — 2026-07-27, 'logging: 0 of 13': an absence claimed by word-grep, a mention-measure that missed the capability; the claim collapsed three times in one morning. The module that doesn't exist yet has no failures; the failures that made it NECESSARY do — so tooth 10's dated-provenance demand survives test-first honestly, exactly as it did for constrain-filters.
traces_to: Law 4 — the acceptance criteria are physics before the behavior exists; survey grows INTO an installed gate
Law 6 — the judge is the inspector's, behind the inspector's write-gate; survey composes it and cannot reach in
Law 8 — the module's first proof must pass a gate it did not write
constrain-filters filed edge (b) — the second instance that turns the judges-before-the-judged move from pattern-candidate into proven pattern

falsifier.proves_green: proof gate: new teeth in test_inspector.py (each filter fire-and-stay-quiet on synthetic survey berths; judge_survey pure and identical through both mouths) under the tester's netns seal. Live gate: the chart-survey ticket builds UNDER these filters — its first berthed packet must pass judges it did not write.
falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: a survey packet with an unresolvable holding address passing either mouth; an empty sought passing; an absence without its measure passing; the two mouths disagreeing (one implementation is the claim); the inspector importing survey (the direction inversion); a filter admitted without dated-failure provenance; the pre-installed set growing speculatively beyond the two measured failure classes (build-minimal holds — the rest arrive through the brick's loop as reality teaches).
falsifier.horizon: re-read when chart-survey builds under these (the dependent ticket, the live gate); when survey's reality teaches a third filter (it arrives through the brick's loop with its own dated failure, by installation); when a third stage installs its judges (the pattern is proven at n=2 — a third instance is routine, not evidence).
